XBMC Media Center 8.10 (codename: Atlantis) Point Release was released on the 14th of November 2008.

XBMC 8.10 (Atlantis) Point Release supports the following
---------------------------------------------------------

_For the cutting edge SVN code, see XBMC Features and Supported Formats/Codecs_

### Supported hardware platforms

*   XBMC for Linux, Mac, and Windows are support on computers of [x86 processor architecture](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X86_architecture)
    .
    *   Minimum requirement is AMD/Intel CPU with SSE support and [OpenGL](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenGL)
         1.4 [GPU (graphics)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPU)
        
*   XBMC for Xbox is compatible with any [modded retail Xbox™](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xbox)
     and Debug/Development-Xboxes

### Platform-independent supported controller periphials and hardware options

*   Controllable via supported Remote Control (depends on platform and remote)
*   Controllable via USB (HID) Mouse (Left/Right/Middle buttons and Wheel supported)
*   Controllable via USB (HID) Touchscreen (as long as the touchscreen emulates a mouse)
*   Controllable via USB (HID) Keyboard (ASCI-keys only, not any multimedia-keys)

### Xbox supported controller periphials and hardware options

*   Fully control XBMC and its features via a [Xbox™ IR DVD-Remote](http://www.xbox.com/sv-SE/hardware/d/dvdplaybackkit/)
    
*   Fully control XBMC and its features via a [Xbox™ game controller](http://www.xbox.com/sv-se/hardware/x/xboxcontroller-s/)
      
    
*   Controllable via USB (HID) Mouse (Left/Right/Middle buttons and Wheel supported) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   Controllable via USB (HID) Keyboard (ASCI-keys only, not any multimedia-keys) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    

### Platform-independent supported output media formats and devices:

*   Widescreen (16:9) and normal-TV (4:3) aspect ratio video output support
*   HDTV (High-Definition) output resolutions (720p, 1080i, 1080p and higher) [#14](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    

### Xbox supported output media formats and devices:

*   TV-output: 50hz/60Hz [NTSC](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ntsc)
    \-M/J (America/Asia) and [PAL](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PAL)
     (Europe/Africa)
*   RCA, SCART, RF Coaxial, S-video, Component/RGB ([adapter available](http://www.xbox.com/en-US/hardware/catalog.aspx?g=203000000&p=1&c=10&s=0&xlm=0&h=0&r=0)
    )
*   VGA-output is also possible via [third-party adapters](http://www.x2vga.com/)
     or [VGA-hacked BIOS](http://xbmc.org/docs/VGA-native.txt)
    
*   [NTSC](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ntsc)
     playback on [PAL](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PAL)
     Xbox/TV and [PAL](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PAL)
     playback on [NTSC](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ntsc)
     Xbox/TV
*   [HDTV](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hdtv)
     support, multiple resolutions 480p/720p/1080i ([Xbox cable-adapter required](http://www.xbox.com/en-US/hardware/catalog.aspx?g=203000000&p=1&c=10&s=0&xlm=0&h=0&r=0)
    )
*   [LCD-display output](http://www.xbmc.xbox-scene.com/forum/showthread.php?t=14370)
     support to view status and control XBMC with TV OFF [#8](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   Analog audio-out (stereo/mono) via phono-connection or scart-adapter
*   Digital audio-out (stereo/mono/surround) SPDIF ([adapter required](http://www.xbox.com/en-US/hardware/catalog.aspx?g=203000000&p=1&c=10&s=0&xlm=0&h=0&r=0)
    )

### Supported physical input media formats and devices:

*   Play media-files directly from a CDs and DVDs (including DVD-Video, VCD/SVCD and Audio-CD/CDDA)[#2](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    *   (Supported CD/DVD formats: ISO 9660 Mode1/2/XA, UDF 1.02 and XDVDFS/CDX)
*   Play media-files directly from any built-in harddisk drive [#4](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   Streaming from a computer/server over a [network](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_area_network)
     via UPnP, SMB/Samba/CIFS, FTP, or XBMSP
    *   Including all NAS (Network Attached Storage) that support UPnP or SMB/SAMBA/CIFS
*   iTunes Music Shares via DAAP (network stream from [Apple iTunes 6.x](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Itunes)
     on Mac or Windows) [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    /[#11](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   Stream supported media-files from the internet (if the stream protocol-format is supported) [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    /[#11](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   Stream media STORED, (NOT COMPRESSED) directly from [RAR](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rar)
     and [ZIP](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZIP_%28file_format%29)
     archives
*   USB Memory Drives and USB Mass Storage Devices (FATX/FAT12/FAT16/FAT32 formated [#13](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    )
    *   Including most USB Mass Storage Devices (like memory-keys/sticks) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
        

  

### Supported file/container formats:

*   Audio-CD (CDDA) playback for normal Audio CDs (including CD-TEXT support) [#7](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   SVCD and VCD (Video CD / CDXA) video, (SVCD/VCD menus are not supported yet)
*   DVD-Video directly from Xbox DVD-ROM drive, Harddisk-drive or network
*   MPEG, MPG, M2V formats (inc. VCD's .dat and .bin and DVD's .vob)
*   MPEG-TS (TY/TS/DV) DVB transport stream format
*   [M2T/M2TS/MTS](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AVCHD)
     ([AVCHD](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AVCHD)
     video format) container [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   [M2TS](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPEG_transport_stream)
     ([Blu-ray](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blu-ray)
     video format) container [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   [EVO](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enhanced_VOB)
     (Enhanced VOB) [HD DVD](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HD_DVD)
     video format container [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   MP4 (MPEG-4 video) container
*   RIFF AVI (AVI 1.0) container
*   OpenDML AVI (AVI 2.0) container [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   [BivX](http://www.morgan-multimedia.com/mmswitch/bivx.htm)
     (AVI with several audio streams) container
*   Microsoft ASF/ASX/WMV/WMA containers [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   [Microsoft DVR-MS (Windows Media Center) containers](http://forum.kodi.tv//showthread.php?t=34)
     [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    /[#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   [QuickTime](http://www.apple.com/quicktime)
     QT/MOV containers [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   FLV and SWF (Adobe/Macromedia Flash Video) containers
*   [NUT](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NUT_Container)
     multimedia container
*   [AVS (Audio Video Standard)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_Video_Standard)
     audio/video containers
*   [Nullsoft Steaming Video (NSV)](http://www.nullsoft.com/nsv/)
     containers [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   [Nullsoft Steaming Audio (NSA)](http://www.nullsoft.com/nsv/)
     containers
*   MPA, MP2, MP3 and WAV containers [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   AAC, M4A, MP4 (MPEG-4 audio) audio containers [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   RealMedia ([Real](http://www.real.com/)
     Video/Audio) RM/RAM/RA/RV/RMVB containers [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   [OGG](http://www.xiph.org/ogg/)
    , OGA, OGM, and OGV containers
*   [Matroska (матрёшка)](http://www.matroska.org/)
     MKV containers [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    
*   VIVO (VIV) containers
*   PVA containers
*   NuppelVideo containers
*   FLI and FLC containers
*   Tracker Mods ([18 formats supported](http://mikmod.raphnet.net/#features)
    ) audio
*   M3U, PLS, CUE and STRM audio/video playlists [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)
    

  

### Supported video codecs:

*   MPEG-1 (VCD/MPG) and MPEG-2 (MPEG/SVCD/DVD/VOB/DV/TY) video
*   [MPEG-4 ASP (H.263)](http://forum.doom9.org/showthread.php?t=73022)
    : [DivX (Pro), OpenDivX, \[http://www.xvid.org XviD](http://www.divx.com/)\
     and [Nero Digital ASP](http://www.nero.com/nerodigital/eng/index.html)\
    \
*   [MPEG-4 AVC - Advanced Video Coding (H.264)](http://forum.doom9.org/showthread.php?t=96059)\
    : [Nero Digital AVC](http://www.nero.com/nerodigital/eng/index.html)\
    , [x264](http://developers.videolan.org/x264.html)\
    , and [DivX AVC](http://www.divx.com/)\
     video [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Microsoft's Windows Media Video v7, v8 and v9 (MSMpeg4/WMV v1, v2, and v3)\
*   [VC-1 (SMPTE 421M)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VC-1)\
    \
*   RealVideo codecs: 1.0, 2.0 (RealPlayer G2), 3.0 (RealPlayer 8.x) and 4.0 (RealPlayer 9.x)\
*   QuickTime 5.0, 6.0, 6.3 video and audio codecs (QDMC / QDM2) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   3ivx D4 / 3vi1 MPEG-4 video (inc. MSZH/ZLIB Compressed-Header containers) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Sorenson v1/v3 (SVQ1/SVQ3) QuickTime video\
*   Apple Graphics (SMC) video\
*   [On2 Technologies](http://www.on2.com/)\
     VP3 (VP3.x), VP4 (VP4.x), VP5 (VP5.x), and VP6 (VP6.2)\
*   [AVS (Audio Video Standard)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_Video_Standard)\
     video codec\
*   [Intel Indeo](http://www.intel.com/labs/archive/indeo.htm)\
     3.1/3.2 (Indeo3)\
*   [NuppelVideo](http://frost.htu.tuwien.ac.at/~roman/nuppelvideo/)\
     (NUV)\
*   VIVO 1.0 and 2.0 (VIV)\
*   ITU H.261 video\
*   Creative Labs YUV (CYUV) video\
*   Supermac Cinepak (CVID) video\
*   ASUS V1 (ASV1) and ASUS V2 (ASV2) video\
*   Autodesk FLI and FLC Animation\
\
  \
\
### Xbox supported video formats and resolutions\
\
This is a comparison table of common video-codecs to show what the Xbox [733Mhz PIII CPU](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pentium_III)\
 can handle:\
\
| Codec / Resolution | 352x240 | 352x288 | 480x480 | 480x576 | 720x480 | 720x576 | 960x540 | 1280x720 | 1920x1080 |\
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\
| [MPEG-1](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPEG-1)<br> / [MPEG-2](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPEG-2) | 1   | 2   | 3   | 4   | 5   | 6   |     | 7\* | 7   |\
| [MPEG-4 ASP (H.263)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPEG-4)<br> (like [DivX](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DivX)<br> or [Xvid](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xvid)<br>) |     |     |     |     |     |     | 8   | 9\* | 10  |\
| [MPEG-4 AVC (H.264)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H264)<br> without [Cabac & Deblocking](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.264#Profiles) |     |     |     |     | \*  | ?   |     |     |     |\
| [MPEG-4 AVC (H.264)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H264)<br> with [Cabac & Deblocking](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H.264#Profiles) |     |     | \*  | ?   |     |     |     | 11  | 12  |\
| [WMV9 (Windows Media Video v3)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WMV)<br> / [VC-1](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/VC-1) |     |     |     |     | \*  | \*  |     |     |     |\
\
" ? " = Undetermined (the Xbox-hardware may or may not be too slow to decode at an acceptable frame-rate)\
\
" \* " = Working with acceptable frame-rates most of the time\
\
1.  a.k.a. NTSC VCD - [More Info](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_CD)\
    \
2.  a.k.a. PAL VCD - [More Info](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_CD)\
    \

    \
4.  a.k.a. PAL SVCD - [More Info](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SVCD)\
    \

    \
6.  a.k.a. PAL DVD-Video - [More Info](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD-Video)\
    \
7.  a.k.a. TS (Transport Stream MPEG-2 Video Stream) - [More Info](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transport_stream)\
    \
8.  a.k.a. HRHD (High Resolution High Definition) - [More Info](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_Resolution_High_Definition)\
    \
9.  a.k.a. DivX HD and XviD HD in 720p\
10.  a.k.a. DivX HD and XviD HD in 1080p\
11.  a.k.a. Quicktime HD, x264, and Nero AG's Nero Digital AVC video in 720p\
12.  a.k.a. Blu-Ray Disc, HD DVD, Quicktime HD, x264, and Nero AG's Nero Digital AVC video in 1080p\

### Supported audio codecs:\
\
*   CDDA (Audio-CD) playback\
*   WAV/WAVE (WAVEform) and PCM audio format\
*   [AIFF](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aiff)\
     (Audio Interchange File Format) audio\
*   MPEG layer I, II, and III (inluding [MP2](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MPEG-1_Audio_Layer_II)\
     and [MP3](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mp3)\
    ) audio [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   [OGG](http://www.xiph.org/ogg/)\
     ([Ogg Vorbis audio codec](http://www.xiph.org/ogg/)\
    )\
*   WMA - Windows Media Audio v1 and v2 (WMA1/2 / DivX Audio v1/v2) [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   WMA - Windows Media Audio v9 (WMA9) (via WMA9 DLL's) [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   [RealNetworks RealAudio](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Realaudio)\
     codecs: 1.0 (14.4), 2.0 (28.8), SIPRO, COOK, DNET and ATRAC3\
*   [AC3](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolby_Digital#Dolby_Digital)\
     2.0 or 5.1 and [Dolby Digital EX](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolby_Digital#Dolby_Digital_EX)\
     6.1 or 7.1 audio in video (AC3 digital cable [S/PDIF](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S/PDIF)\
     48Khz pass-through)\
*   [Dolby Digital](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolby_Digital)\
     AC3 and AC3-WAV/AC3-CDDA 2.0 and 5.1 audio in video software decoded to stereo analog-out\
*   [DTS (Digital Theater System)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Theater_System)\
     5.1 and [DTS-ES](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Theater_System#DTS_variants)\
     6.1 audio in DVD-Video (DTS digital cable [S/PDIF](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S/PDIF)\
     48Khz pass-through)\
*   [DTS](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Theater_System)\
     (DTS and DTS-WAV/DTS-CDDA) 44.1Khz/48Khz audio in DVD-Video (software decoded)\
*   [AAC (Advanced Audio Coding)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Audio_Coding)\
     profiles: Main, LC, HE, LTP, LD, ER, and [aacPlus v1/v2 (AAC+ SBR/PS)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advanced_Audio_Coding#Extensions_.26_improvements)\
     audio [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   M4A and MP4 (MPEG-4 Audio) (including Nero Digital MP4) [#5](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   [AVS (Audio Video Standard)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Audio_Video_Standard)\
     audio codec\
*   [FLAC](http://flac.sourceforge.net/)\
     (Free Lossless Audio Codec) audio\
*   [WavPack](http://www.wavpack.com/)\
     lossless audio\
*   [MPC](http://www.musepack.net/)\
     (Musepack, a.k.a. Mpeg+) lossless audio [#6](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   [APE](http://www.monkeysaudio.com/)\
     (Monkey's Audio) lossless audio\
*   [SHN](http://www.etree.org/shnutils/shorten/)\
     (Shorten) lossless audio\
*   [ALAC](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ALAC)\
     (Apple Lossless Audio Codec) lossless audio [#6](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   [MIDI](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midi)\
     music using [Timidity](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TiMidity)\
    \
*   Tracker Mod's audio, see list below:\
    *   [Adlib](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AdLib)\
         (AdLib and Sound Blaster OPL2/OPL3 and Dual OPL2/OPL3) FM audio\
    *   [SID](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS_Technology_SID)\
         (Commodore 64 tunes) audio\
    *   [YM](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atari_ST)\
         (ATARI ST) audio\
    *   [NSF](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nsf)\
         (Nintendo NES Sound Format) audio\
    *   [SPC](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SPC700_sound_format)\
         (SPC700) audio\
    *   [GYM](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/.GYM)\
         (SEGA Genesis) audio\
    *   [ADX/AST/ADP/DSP/YMF/HPS](http://www.halleyscometsoftware.com/in_cube.html)\
         [CRI MiddleWare](http://www.cri-mw.com/example/example_e.htm)\
         and Gamecube [ADPCM](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ADPCM)\
        ) audio\
    *   ([MOD](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Module_file)\
        /AMF/669/DMF/DSM/FAR/GDM/IMF/IT/M15/MED/OKT/S3M/STM/SFX/ULT/UNI/XM)\
\
  \
\
### Supported picture/image formats:\
\
*   CBR/CBZ comic books (RAR/ZIP archives renamed)\
*   BMP picture/image\
*   JPG/JPEG picture/image\
*   GIF picture/image\
*   ICO picture/image\
*   PCX picture/image\
*   PNG picture/image\
*   RAW picture/image\
*   TIF/TIFF picture/image\
*   TGA picture/image\
\
  \
\
### Features available for video playback:\
\
*   Full-screen playback display of all supported video formats/containers via a TV\
*   Auto PAL50/PAL60-switching support and auto 4:3/16:9-switching support\
*   Framerate Conversion (23.98<->25fps), another NTSC <-> PAL workaround solution\
*   SQL database with view by file/genre/actor/year/title, sort by year/name/rating and search functions\
*   Selectable options from OSD (On Screen Display) Control Panel during playback\
*   FFWD (fast-forward) and RWD (rewind [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    ), and PAUSE in AVI/OGM/MKV/MPEG/MPG media\
*   MPlayer time-based (30sec/5min) or percent-based (2%/10%) seeking forward and backward\
*   Video-Autorun, auto-plays VCD/SVCD/DVD/CD's with video file(s) upon insert\
*   DVD-video playback with menus (from DVD, harddrive, network, as IFO/VOB or ISO/IMG DVD-images) [#12](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Play supported video files directly from ISO, BIN, IMG, NRG and BIN CD/DVD-images\
*   Subtitle support (embedded and external)\
    *   AQTitle/AQT, ASS/SSA, CC, JacoSub, MicroDVD, MPsub, PJS, RT, SMI, SRT, SUB, VobSub, VPlayer\
    *   JSS, MLP [#11](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
        \
*   Play internet files/streams from HTTP and MMS (Microsoft Media Streaming Protocol) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    /[#11](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Play RealMedia internet steams of HTTP + RTSP/RDT (Real Data Transport Protocol) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    /[#11](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   [Nullsoft Streaming Video (NSV)](http://www.nullsoft.com/nsv/)\
     internet-streams (only if VP3+MP3), (Nullsoft TV a.k.a. [NTV](http://www.nullsoft.com/ntv/)\
    ) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    /[#11](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Streaming video from a [TiVo](http://www.tivo.com/)\
     DVR box over network (requires hacked TiVo running [ccXStream](http://osdn.dl.sourceforge.net/sourceforge/xbplayer/ccxstream-1.0.15-tivo.tar.gz)\
    ) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Streaming video from a [ReplayTV](http://www.replaytv.com/)\
     (4500, 5000 or 5500 series) DVR box over network [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Internet Movie information lookup for movie-info and thumbnails\
    *   Can also extract a specific URL from an nfo file with same file-name as the movie\
*   Optional media file and/or folder thumbnails for easy localization (see Artwork)\
*   Party Mode playlists and playlist editor.\
*   Stack multi-file videos option, show/play files with 90% name similarity as one\
*   Support for local moving trailer files (using the naming standard: "moviename-trailer.avi")\
*   EDL (commercial skipping) and SceneMarker support using chapter files\
    *   EDL (Edit Decision List)\
    *   ComSkip .txt (with framerate, like Comskip generates)\
    *   VideoReDo\
    *   SnapStream Beyond TV Smart Chapters (a.k.a. smartskip)\
*   Switch between multiple audio streams/tracks in DVD-Video, AVI, OGM and MKV/Matroska\
    *   Left, Right Mono and Stereo channel selection available for all two channel audio-streams\
*   Multiple video-rendering options to optimize playback of your video-formats\
*   Different Post-Processing filters for better video quality [#11](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Flicker-filter (optional video flicker-filter with five levels, disabled by default)\
*   Soften-filter (optional filter to decrease video sharpness and thus artifacts)\
*   De-interlace filter (for interlaced video) implementation option\
*   Brightness/Contrast/Gamma controls (only for HighQuality Pixelshader)\
*   Video resizing/scaling and zooming functions\
*   Screenshot capture function (including video overlay support and OSD)\
*   AC3 (Dolby Digital EAX) 2.0, 5.1 and 7.1 pass-through from video to SP/DIF AC3 output\
*   AC3 (Dolby Digital) 5.1 -> 2.0 software-decoding to PCM stereo or mono out\
*   DTS (Digital Theatre Sound ES) pass-through from video to S/PDIF DTS output\
*   Option to output mono or stereo to all speakers (for 5.1 surround speakers)\
\
  \
\
### Features available for audio playback:\
\
*   Playback of all supported audio-formats via a TV or external audio-receiver/amplifier\
*   SQL database with view music by Top100/Albums/Tracks/Artists/Filenames or Recent Albums\
    *   Also option to sort by Track/Filename/Date or Size and search functions\
*   Karaoke CDG-file display for music files with audio-visualization overlay support\
*   [CDDB](http://www.freedb.org/)\
     album lookup support when playing Audio-CD's (done via [freedb.org](http://www.freedb.org/)\
    )\
*   Party Mode playlists and playlist editor.\
*   Gapless, Crossfade, and Preamp (pre-amplification) playback support options\
*   [ReplayGain](http://www.replaygain.org/)\
     "MetaData" applification/normalization (loudness control) support\
*   Thumbnail and album information lookup for Audio-CD's (done via [AMG/Allmusic.com](http://www.allmusic.com/)\
    )\
*   Display embedded tumbnails/icons (album artwork) if integrated into a MP3 or AAC file\
*   Optional custom file and/or folder thumbnails for easy localization (see Artwork)\
*   Audio-Autorun, auto-plays CDDA and music DVD/CD's with audio file(s) upon insert\
*   Play internet-files/streams from HTTP and MMS (Microsoft Media Streaming Protocol) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    /[#11](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Play RealMedia internet steams of HTTP + RTSP/RDT (Real Data Transport Protocol) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    /[#11](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Play soundtracks ripped by/in Xbox dashboard (add path "soundtrack://" to XML)\
*   Play supported audio files directly from BIN, IMG, NRG and ISO CD/DVD-images\
*   Reads [ID3v1](http://www.id3.org/id3v1.html)\
    /[ID3v2](http://www.id3.org/easy.html)\
    /[ID666](http://www.alpha-ii.com/snesmusic/files/spc_file_format.txt)\
    /APEv1/[APEv2](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/APEv2_tag)\
     info-tags from audio/music-files\
*   M3U and PLS audio playlists (inc. option to create/save M3U audio-playlists)\
*   [SHOUTcast](http://www.shoutcast.com/)\
     Internet Radio (MP3 .pls playlists) playback support\
*   Local/native [SHOUTcast](http://www.shoutcast.com/)\
     recording (to MP3) onto the Xbox harddrive\
*   last.fm (AudioScrobbler) online-radio submission and playback/streaming support\
*   Audio Visualizations (several visual generators and a spectrum analyser)\
*   FF (fast-forward) and RW (rewind), and PAUSE during audio playback/visualization\
*   Option to output mono or stereo to all speakers (for 5.1 surround speakers)\
\
  \
\
### Features available for picture/image viewing:\
\
*   Full-screen display of all supported picture and image formats via a TV\
*   Picture slideshow, including option for adding recursive to slideshows\
*   Picture thumbnails (automatically generated on demand)\
*   Folder thumbnails (automatically generated after entered that folder)\
*   View pictures directly from ISO, IMG, NRG and BIN CD/DVD-images\
*   Picture Zooming, rotate, move around, info, pause, next/previous picture\
*   [Kodak PictureCD compatible](http://www.kodak.com/eknec/PageQuerier.jhtml?pq-path=2/3/9/511&pq-locale=en_US)\
     (auto-launches slideshow on CD insert) [#2](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Auto-launches picture CD/DVD on insert if images in root directory\
\
  \
\
### Features available for launching games and applications (dashboard):\
\
#### My Programs interface features in XBMC for Xbox:\
\
*   Dashboard replacement mode, launch other Xbox software applications ("XBE" executables)\
    *   (including Xbox games, console-emulators, applications and other dashboards, etc.)\
*   Optional custom thumbnails for folders and the executable, (see Artwork for info)\
*   Display embedded tumbnails/icons that are integrated into most Xbox executables for Xbox games\
*   Video Mode Switching to force launching a game a specific video-mode (PAL, PAL60, NTSC, etc.)\
*   Flicker-Filter settings for Xbox games, (creates a patched copy of all default.xbe with new setting)\
\
  \
\
#### Xored Trainer Engine (gaming cheats) in XBMC for Xbox:\
\
*   Xored ETM/XBTF Trainer Engine enable "training" of games to cheat and/or add new functions to Xbox games [#10](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Xored ETM/XBTF Trainer Engine cannot be used to cheat on XLink Kai (as disabled when logged on to XLink Kai)\
\
  \
\
### Other and generic Graphical User Interface (GUI) features:\
\
*   Controllable via a [Remote Control](http://www.xbox.com/sv-SE/hardware/d/dvdplaybackkit/Xbox%E2%84%A2)\
    , a [game-pad](http://www.xbox.com/sv-se/hardware/x/xboxcontroller-s/)\
    , USB keyboard and/or USB mouse\
*   Virtual-Keyboard for manual video/music database searches and settings configurations\
*   Flexible XML based skinning-engine with GUI skin-switching (and many skins available)\
*   Range of different view modes (supports up to 10 custom skinner created views)\
*   Context Menu feature (mapped by default to the TITLE button on the remote)\
*   View file media listing By List, By Small Icons or By Large Icons option\
*   "My Files" file-manager, move/copy/delete local and copy from network\
*   "My Weather" weather forecast feature (done via [The Weather Channel](http://www.weather.com/)\
    )\
*   Several screensavers on configurable timer in GUI to choose from\
*   RSS feed in main menu (you can manually disable or change feed in RssFeeds.xml)\
*   [Python](http://www.python.org/)\
     Script Interpreter Engine (execute/run Python scripts from within XBMC)\
*   Idle shutdown-timer, which shutdown XBMC when idle, configurable timer through GUI\
*   Non-idle sleep timer, shutdown XBMC even if not idle after specific set manually\
*   Flicker-filter (optional GUI flicker-filter with five levels, high enabled by default)\
*   Language (XML) files for translated GUI (over 30+ languages so far), switch from GUI\
*   International-language fonts for the GUI (via TTF-Fonts, configurable in UI-Settings)\
*   GUI and video calibration (including storing calibration settings per resolution)\
*   Displays system info under Settings (Build date, free space, IP, temperature)\
*   Screenshot capture function, to snap shots of GUI (inc. video overlay support)\
*   Configurable memory cache buffer for video/audio playback, configured in GUI\
\
  \
\
### Other non-GUI features, functions and options:\
\
*   Fully re-mappable keys for [DVD Remote](http://www.xbox.com/sv-SE/hardware/d/dvdplaybackkit/Xbox%E2%84%A2)\
     and the [controller/game-pad](http://www.xbox.com/sv-se/hardware/x/xboxcontroller-s/)\
     (via Keymap.xml)\
    *   Including the possibility to map and use all RCA-5 IR codes from a universal remote\
*   Auto-detection of UDF 1.02, XDVDFS/CDX and ISO9660 - mode1/mode2/XA [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Auto-launch Xbox game-disc on insert with enable/disable optional from within GUI\
*   Advanced and expert options available via an optional AdvancedSettings.xml file\
*   Built-in Web-Server for remote control of XBMC (http//:xboxIPaddressHere.asp)\
*   Built-in HTTP API interface so you can build custom remote control applications\
*   Built-in FTP-Server, connect to it via an FTP client to copy files to/from Xbox harddrive\
*   Supports Static-IP/Subnetmask/DNS/WINS and alternative DHCP-client for auto config\
*   Clock/date synchronization from a (NT SNTP) Time Server on the network/internet\
*   Harddrive (HDD) spindown on idle (spin-down disks when XBMC is idle in menu) [#1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:XBMC_8.10_point_release#Notes)\
    \
*   Error Recovery Mode (Emergency Recovery Console) - Enables the FTP-server if get corrupt XBMC system-files.\
\
  \
\
Notes\
-----\
\
**1.** Experimental, unfinished, unstable, buggy and/or limited  \
**2.** Most Xbox DVD-ROM drives are very picky with CD/DVD media disks, see FAQ  \
**3.** XBMC currently only have DVD VOB and IFO parsing support, (no menu support)  \
**3.** Xbox's [FATX](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FATX)\
 harddrive file-system has file & folder name/character limitations, see FAQ  \
**5.** [DRM (Digital Rights Management)](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digital_Rights_Management)\
 protected files are not yet supported by XBMC  \
**6.** Exclusive to our integrated audio/music-player (PAPlayer)  \
**7.** Samsung DVD-ROM drive only (and maybe some PC DVD-ROM drives)  \
**8.** For LCD-display add-on mods compatible with XBMC see [here](http://www.xbmc.xbox-scene.com/forum/showthread.php?t=14370)\
  \
**9.** Xlink Kai tunneling-engine running on networked computer with internet-access is required.  \
**10.** Xored ETM/XBTF Trainer Engine is only developed/maintained/supported by [Team Xored](http://forums.maxconsole.net/forumdisplay.php?f=44)\
.  \
**11.** Exclusive to our MPlayer-based media-player (only available in XBMC for Xbox).  \
**12.** Exclusive to our DVDPlayer (FFmpeg-based) video-player.  \
**13.** Exclusive to XBMC for Xbox (XBMC running nativly on Xbox game-console).  \
**14.** Only limited by the hardware and operating-system that XBMC is running on.  \

# Panel Container - Official Kodi Wiki

Panel Container
===============

From Official Kodi Wiki

[Jump to navigation](https://kodi.wiki/view/Panel_Container#mw-head)
 [Jump to search](https://kodi.wiki/view/Panel_Container#searchInput)

See also: **[Add-on development](https://kodi.wiki/view/Add-on_development "Add-on development")
** and **[Skinning](https://kodi.wiki/view/Skinning "Skinning")
**

The panel container is one of several containers used to display items from file lists in various ways. The panel container is very flexible - it's essentially a multi-column list. The layout of the items is very flexible and is up to the skinner.

Example
-------

<control type="panel" id="52">
	<left>190</left>
	<top>100</top>
	<width>485</width>
	<height>425</height>
	<onleft>9000</onleft>
	<onright>60</onright>
	<onup>52</onup>
	<ondown>52</ondown>
	<scrolltime tween="sine" easing="out">200</scrolltime>
	<autoscroll>true</autoscroll>
	<viewtype label="536">icon</viewtype>
	<pagecontrol>60</pagecontrol>
	<include>contentpanelslide</include>
	<itemlayout height="150" width="120">
		<control type="image">
			<left>10</left>
			<top>10</top>
			<width>100</width>
			<height>100</height>
			<texture>$INFO\[ListItem.Icon\]</texture>
		</control>
		<control type="image">
			<left>80</left>
			<top>75</top>
			<width>32</width>
			<height>32</height>
			<texture>$INFO\[ListItem.Overlay\]</texture>
		</control>
		<control type="label">
			<left>0</left>
			<top>115</top>
			<width>110</width>
			<height>22</height>
			<font>font13</font>
			<selectedcolor>green</selectedcolor>
			<align>center</align>
			<label>$INFO\[ListItem.Label\]</label>
		</control>
	</itemlayout>
	<focusedlayout height="150" width="120">
		<control type="image">
			<width>110</width>
			<height>110</height>
			<left>5</left>
			<top>5</top>
			<texture>folder-focus.png</texture>
			<animation effect="zoom" end="0,0,120,120" time="100">focus</animation>
		</control>
		<control type="image">
			<left>10</left>
			<top>10</top>
			<width>100</width>
			<height>100</height>
			<texture>$INFO\[ListItem.Icon\]</texture>
			<animation effect="zoom" end="5,5,110,110" time="100">focus</animation>
		</control>
		<control type="image">
			<left>80</left>
			<top>75</top>
			<width>32</width>
			<height>32</height>
			<texture>$INFO\[ListItem.Overlay\]</texture>
			<animation effect="slide" end="5,5" time="100">focus</animation>
		</control>
		<control type="label">
			<left>0</left>
			<top>120</top>
			<width>110</width>
			<height>22</height>
			<font>font13</font>
			<selectedcolor>green</selectedcolor>
			<align>center</align>
			<label>$INFO\[ListItem.Label\]</label>
		</control>
	</focusedlayout>
</control>

### Available tags

In addition to the [Default Control Tags](https://kodi.wiki/view/Default_Control_Tags "Default Control Tags")
, the following tags are also available. Note that each tag is lower case only. This is important, as XML tags are case-sensitive.

|     |     |
| --- | --- |Available tags
| Tag | Description |
| `<viewtype label="">…</viewtype>` | The type of view, valid values are: `list`, `icon`, `wide`, `wrap`, `biglist`, `bigicon`, `bigwide`, `bigwrap`, `info` and `biginfo`. The `label` attribute indicates the label that will be used in the "View As" control within the GUI. It is localizable via strings.po. This tag has no effect on the view itself, it is simply used by Kodi when switching skins to automatically select a view with a similar layout; skinners should try to set it to best describe the layout provided. |
| `<orientation>…</orientation>` | The orientation of the panel, defaults to `vertical`. |
| `<pagecontrol>…</pagecontrol>` | Used to set the `id` of the page control used to control that panel. |
| `<scrolltime tween="" easing="">…</scrolltime>` | The time (in ms) to scroll from one item to another, by default this is 200ms. The panel will scroll smoothly from one item to another as needed; set it to zero to disable the smooth scrolling. The scroll movement can be further adjusted by selecting one of the available **[tween methods](https://kodi.wiki/view/Tweeners "Tweeners")<br>**. |
| `<itemlayout height="" width="">…</itemlayout>` | Specifies the **[container item layout](https://kodi.wiki/view/Container_Item_Layout "Container Item Layout")<br>** for the list, and requires both the `width` and `height` attributes to be set. It will contain as many label and image controls as needed. |
| `<focusedlayout height="" width="">…</focusedlayout>` | Specifies the **[container item layout](https://kodi.wiki/view/Container_Item_Layout "Container Item Layout")<br>** for items that have focus in the list, and requires both the `width` and `height` attributes to be set. It will contain as many label and image controls as needed. |
| `<content>…</content>` | Used to set the **[static list content](https://kodi.wiki/view/Static_List_Content "Static List Content")<br>** that the panel will contain, allowing the skinner to create a panel anywhere they want with a static set of content, as a useful counterpart to the `grouplist` control. |
| `<preloaditems>…</preloaditems>` | Used in association with the **[background image loader](https://kodi.wiki/view/Archive:Background_Image_Loader "Archive:Background Image Loader")<br>**. |
| `<autoscroll>…</autoscroll>` | Used to make the container scroll automatically, accepts the boolean values of either `true` or `false`. |

Retrieved from "[https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=Panel\_Container&oldid=242948](https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=Panel_Container&oldid=242948)
"

HOW-TO:Fix new controller detected dialog
-----------------------------------------

*   [![Kodi shows an "Unknown controller detected" message](https://kodi.wiki/images/0/0b/NVIDIA_SHIELD_-_New_controller_detected.jpg)](https://kodi.wiki/view/File:NVIDIA_SHIELD_-_New_controller_detected.jpg "Kodi shows an "Unknown controller detected" message")
    
    Kodi shows an "Unknown controller detected" message
    

This can happen the first time you press a button on the NVidia Shield controller.

To fix this, select No in the dialog. If you select Yes, the dialog will be shown again.

  

HOW-TO:Fix double button presses
--------------------------------

*   [![The NVidia SHIELD controller shows up as two devices](https://kodi.wiki/images/c/c3/NVidia_Shield_peripherals_list.jpg)](https://kodi.wiki/view/File:NVidia_Shield_peripherals_list.jpg "The NVidia SHIELD controller shows up as two devices")
    
    The NVidia SHIELD controller shows up as two devices
    

To fix double button presses, remove the button map for the second device. See [HOW-TO:Share button maps](https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Share_button_maps "HOW-TO:Share button maps")
, but instead of sharing the XML file, delete it and restart Kodi.

# Default control tags - Official Kodi Wiki

Default control tags
====================

From Official Kodi Wiki

[Jump to navigation](https://kodi.wiki/view/Default_control_tags#mw-head)
 [Jump to search](https://kodi.wiki/view/Default_control_tags#searchInput)

Here are the tags and attributes available for all controls. **Note that they're all lowercase, as XML is case sensitive**.

Contents
--------

*   [1 Tags available to all controls](https://kodi.wiki/view/Default_control_tags#Tags_available_to_all_controls)
    
*   [2 Tags available to focusable controls](https://kodi.wiki/view/Default_control_tags#Tags_available_to_focusable_controls)
    
*   [3 Similar page names](https://kodi.wiki/view/Default_control_tags#Similar_page_names)
    
*   [4 See also](https://kodi.wiki/view/Default_control_tags#See_also)
    

### Tags available to all controls

| Tag(s) | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| description | Only used to make things clear for the skinner. Not read by Kodi at all. |
| type | The type of control. |
| id  | Specifies the control's id. The value this takes depends on the control type, and the window that you are using the control on. There are special control id's that must be present in each window. Any other controls that the skinner adds can be any id they like. Any controls that the skinner specifies content needs not have an id unless it's needed for animation purposes. For instance, most image and label controls don't need an id if the skinner specifies they're content. |
| left | Specifies where the left edge of the control should be drawn, relative to it's parent's left edge. If an "r" is included (eg 180r) then the measurement is taken from the parent's right edge (in the left direction). This can be an absolute value or a %. |
| top | Specifies where the top edge of the control should be drawn, relative to it's parent's top edge. If an "r" is included (eg 180r) then the measurement is taken from the parent's bottom edge (in the up direction). This can be an absolute value or a %. |
| right | Specifies where the right edge of the control should be drawn. This can be an absolute value or a %. |
| bottom | Specifies where the bottom edge of the control should be drawn. This can be an absolute value or a %. |
| centerleft | Aligns the control horizontally at the given coordinate measured from the left side of the parent control. This can be an absolute value or a %. |
| centerright | Aligns the control horizontally at the given coordinate measured from the right side of the parent control. This can be an absolute value or a %. |
| centertop | Aligns the control vertically at the given coordinate measured from the top side of the parent control. This can be an absolute value or a %. |
| centerbottom | Aligns the control vertically at the given coordinate measured from the bottom side of the parent control. This can be an absolute value or a %. |
| width | Specifies the width that should be used to draw the control. You can use <width>auto</width> for labels (in grouplists) and button/togglebutton controls. |
| height | Specifies the height that should be used to draw the control. |
| visible | Specifies a condition as to when this control will be visible. Can be true, false, or a condition. See [Conditional Visibility](https://kodi.wiki/view/Conditional_Visibility "Conditional Visibility")<br> for more information. Defaults to true. |
| animation | Specifies the animation to be run when the control enters a particular state. See [Animating your skin](https://kodi.wiki/view/Animating_your_skin "Animating your skin")<br> for more information. |
| camera | Specifies the location (relative to the parent's coordinates) of the camera. Useful for the 3D animations such as rotatey. Format is `<camera x="20" y="30" />`. 'r' values and % are also supported. |
| depth | Specifies the 3D stereoscopic depth of a control. possible values range from -1.0 to 1.0, which brings control "to back" and "to front". |
| colordiffuse | This specifies the color to be used for the texture basis. It's in hex AARRGGBB format. If you define `<colordiffuse>FFFF00FF</colordiffuse>` (magenta), the image will be given a magenta tint when rendered. Defaults to FFFFFFFF (no tint). You can also specify this as a name from the [colour theme](https://kodi.wiki/view/Colour_themes "Colour themes")<br>. |

[![](https://kodi.wiki/images/f/f3/Control-positioning.jpg)](https://kodi.wiki/view/File:Control-positioning.jpg)

### Tags available to focusable controls

In addition, any control that is focusable (e.g. a buttoncontrol) will have the following tags available.

| Tags | Definition |
| --- | --- |
| onup | Specifies the `<id>` of the control that should be moved to when the user moves up off this control. Can point to a control group (which remembers previous focused items). |
| ondown | Specifies the `<id>` of the control that should be moved to when the user moves down off this control. Can point to a control group (which remembers previous focused items). |
| onleft | Specifies the `<id>` of the control that should be moved to when the user moves left off this control. Can point to a control group (which remembers previous focused items). |
| onright | Specifies the `<id>` of the control that should be moved to when the user moves right off this control. Can point to a control group (which remembers previous focused items). |
| onback | Specifies the `<id>` of the control that should be focussed when the user presses the back key. Can point to a control group (which remembers previous focused items). |
| oninfo | Specifies the built-in function that should be executed when the user presses the info key. |
| onfocus | Specifies the built-in function that should be executed when the control is focussed. |
| onunfocus | Specifies the built-in function that should be executed when the control is loses focus. |
| hitrect | Specifies the location and size of the "focus area" of this control (relative to the parent's coordinates) used by the mouse cursor. Format is `<hitrect x="20" y="30" w="50" h="10" />` |
| hitrectcolor | This adds the ability to visualize hitrects for controls. When visible and there's a <hitrectcolor> tag, it will paint a colored rectangle over the actual control. Colors can be specified in AARRGGBB format or a name from the color theme. |
| enable | Specifies a condition as to when this control will be enabled. Can be true, false, or a condition. See [Conditional Visibility](https://kodi.wiki/view/Conditional_Visibility "Conditional Visibility")<br> for more information. Defaults to true. |
| pulseonselect | This specifies whether or not a button type will "pulse" when it has focus. This is done by varying the alpha channel of the button. Defaults to true. |

# HOW-TO:PlayStation 4 controller - Official Kodi Wiki

HOW-TO:PlayStation 4 controller
===============================

From Official Kodi Wiki

[Jump to navigation](https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:PlayStation_4_controller#mw-head)
 [Jump to search](https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:PlayStation_4_controller#searchInput)

|     |     |     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [![](https://kodi.wiki/images/a/aa/Home_icon_grey.png)](https://kodi.wiki/view/Main_Page "Main Page") |     |     | ![▶](https://kodi.wiki/images/5/5f/TriangleArrow-Right.png) [Remote controls](https://kodi.wiki/view/Remote_controls "Remote controls")<br>  <br>![▶](https://kodi.wiki/images/5/5f/TriangleArrow-Right.png) [Games](https://kodi.wiki/view/Games "Games") | ![▶](https://kodi.wiki/images/5/5f/TriangleArrow-Right.png) [Game controllers](https://kodi.wiki/view/Game_controllers "Game controllers") | ![▶](https://kodi.wiki/images/5/5f/TriangleArrow-Right.png) **HOW-TO:PlayStation 4 controller** |

The PlayStation 4 controller has a quirk where triggers send both a digital button press and an analog value. This causes problems when mapping triggers in the controller window.

  
The steps here are also documented in the article [HOW-TO:Fix buttons skipped while mapping](https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Fix_buttons_skipped_while_mapping "HOW-TO:Fix buttons skipped while mapping")
.

  

Symptoms
--------

*   [![First, Kodi prompts you to press Left Trigger](https://kodi.wiki/images/3/32/Mapping_a_trigger.jpg)](https://kodi.wiki/view/File:Mapping_a_trigger.jpg "First, Kodi prompts you to press Left Trigger")
    
    First, Kodi prompts you to press Left Trigger
    
*   [![Pressing Left Trigger causes Right Trigger to be skipped](https://kodi.wiki/images/1/17/Trigger_was_skipped_2.jpg)](https://kodi.wiki/view/File:Trigger_was_skipped_2.jpg "Pressing Left Trigger causes Right Trigger to be skipped")
    
    Pressing Left Trigger causes Right Trigger to be skipped
    

  

Solution
--------

*   [![Use the "Ignore Input" utility to ignore the extra button presses](https://kodi.wiki/images/b/b1/Ignore_input.jpg)](https://kodi.wiki/view/File:Ignore_input.jpg "Use the "Ignore Input" utility to ignore the extra button presses")
    
    Use the "Ignore Input" utility to ignore the extra button presses
    
*   [![When the dialog opens, press both triggers LIGHTLY](https://kodi.wiki/images/7/78/Ignore_input_dialog.jpg)](https://kodi.wiki/view/File:Ignore_input_dialog.jpg "When the dialog opens, press both triggers LIGHTLY")
    
    When the dialog opens, press both triggers LIGHTLY
    
*   [![When the number shows up, release the trigger](https://kodi.wiki/images/8/89/Buttons_were_ignored.jpg)](https://kodi.wiki/view/File:Buttons_were_ignored.jpg "When the number shows up, release the trigger")
    
    When the number shows up, release the trigger
    

If you continue pressing the trigger after the button is detected, it will ignore the axis too. In this case, the trigger can't be mapped at all. Simply cancel the dialog and try again.

Once Kodi knows to ignore the digital button presses, the trigger's analog values can be mapped successfully.

  

See also
--------

*   **[HOW-TO:Configure controllers](https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Configure_controllers "HOW-TO:Configure controllers")
    **
*   **[HOW-TO:Share button maps](https://kodi.wiki/view/HOW-TO:Share_button_maps "HOW-TO:Share button maps")
    **

Retrieved from "[https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=HOW-TO:PlayStation\_4\_controller&oldid=223301](https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=HOW-TO:PlayStation_4_controller&oldid=223301)
"

# Template:TemplateData header/doc - Official Kodi Wiki

Template:TemplateData header/doc
================================

From Official Kodi Wiki

< [Template:TemplateData header](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header "Template:TemplateData header")

[Jump to navigation](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header/doc#mw-head)
 [Jump to search](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header/doc#searchInput)

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| ![](https://kodi.wiki/images/4/45/Emblem-important-yellow.png) | **_NOTICE:_ This is a documentation subpage for [Template:TemplateData header](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header "Template:TemplateData header")<br>:**  <br>It contains usage information, categories and other content that is not part of the original template page. |

  

The {{[TemplateData header](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header "Template:TemplateData header")
}} template inserts a brief header for the TemplateData section, and adds the page to [Category:Templates using TemplateData](https://kodi.wiki/view/Category:Templates_using_TemplateData "Category:Templates using TemplateData")
.

Contents
--------

*   [1 Usage](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header/doc#Usage)
    
*   [2 Example](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header/doc#Example)
    
*   [3 Parameters](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header/doc#Parameters)
    
*   [4 See also](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header/doc#See_also)
    

Usage
-----

\== TemplateData == {{TemplateData header}} <templatedata>{ … }</templatedata> <!-- Note: Section headers of == Parameters == or == Usage == may also be used. -->

Use {{[TemplateData header](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header "Template:TemplateData header")
|Template name}} to display a name for the template other than the default, which is [{{BASEPAGENAME}}](http://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Help:Magic_words#Page_names "mw:Help:Magic words")
. Do _not_ add namespace `Template:`.

This is the [TemplateData](http://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:TemplateData "mw:Extension:TemplateData")
 for this template used by [TemplateWizard](http://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:TemplateWizard "mw:Extension:TemplateWizard")
, [VisualEditor](http://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:VisualEditor "mw:Extension:VisualEditor")
 and other tools.

**TemplateData for Template name**

Use {{[TemplateData header](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header "Template:TemplateData header")
|nolink=1}} to omit the wikilink from the word 'TemplateData' in the header text, for instances where it is already linked outside this template.

This is the TemplateData for this template used by [TemplateWizard](http://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:TemplateWizard "mw:Extension:TemplateWizard")
, [VisualEditor](http://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:VisualEditor "mw:Extension:VisualEditor")
 and other tools.

**TemplateData for TemplateData header**

Use {{[TemplateData header](https://kodi.wiki/view/Template:TemplateData_header "Template:TemplateData header")
|noheader=1}} to omit the first sentence of the header text.

**TemplateData for TemplateData header**

Example
-------

Using a collapse box for &lsqbr;&lsqbr;Template:User&rsqbr;&rsqbr;:

{{Collapse top|title=TemplateData}} {{TemplateData header|User}} <templatedata>{ "description": "This template is used to create a link to a user's user page, talk page, and contributions, and generates a special notification (aka 'ping').", "params": { "1": { "label": "User name", "type": "string", "required": true, "description": "The user name that you want to create links to and notify.", "aliases":\[ "user" \] }, "separator": { "label": "Separator", "description": "Used to change the separator between the links. If unused, defaults to a dot." } } }</templatedata> {{Collapse bottom}}

Parameters
----------

This is the [TemplateData](http://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:TemplateData "mw:Extension:TemplateData")
 for this template used by [TemplateWizard](http://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:TemplateWizard "mw:Extension:TemplateWizard")
, [VisualEditor](http://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Extension:VisualEditor "mw:Extension:VisualEditor")
 and other tools.

**TemplateData for TemplateData header**

<templatedata>{

 "description": "Inserts a brief header for the template data section. Adds the page to ",
 "params": {
   "1": {
     "label": "Template name",
     "description": "Used to display a name for the template other than the default, which is TemplateData header.",
     "type": "string",
     "required": false
   },
   "nolink": {
     "label": "No link",
     "description": "Assigning any value to this parameter will omit cause the template to omit the wikilink from the word \\"TemplateData\\" in the header text, for instances where it is already linked outside this template.",
     "type": "string",
     "required": false
   },
   "noheader": {
     "label": "No header",
     "description": "Assigning any value to this parameter will cause the template to omit the first sentence of the header text.",
     "type": "string",
     "required": false
   }
 }

}</templatedata>

See also
--------

*   [Category:Templates using TemplateData](https://kodi.wiki/view/Category:Templates_using_TemplateData "Category:Templates using TemplateData")
    

Retrieved from "[https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=Template:TemplateData\_header/doc&oldid=242993](https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=Template:TemplateData_header/doc&oldid=242993)
"

Al Jazeera

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| ![icon.png](http://mirrors.kodi.tv/addons/leia/plugin.video.aljazeera/icon.png) |     |
| **Author:** | Jonathan Beluch (jbel) |
| **Type:** | [Video](https://kodi.wiki/view/Category:Video_add-ons "Category:Video add-ons") |

|     |     |     |     |     |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [![](https://kodi.wiki/images/a/aa/Home_icon_grey.png)](https://kodi.wiki/view/Main_Page "Main Page") |     |     | ![▶](https://kodi.wiki/images/5/5f/TriangleArrow-Right.png) [Add-ons](https://kodi.wiki/view/Add-ons "Add-ons") | ![▶](https://kodi.wiki/images/5/5f/TriangleArrow-Right.png) **Al Jazeera** |

"Drawing on the legacy of the groundbreaking Al Jazeera Arabic channel, Al Jazeera English was launched on November 15, 2006 to more than 80 million households worldwide.  
  
 The 24-hour news and current affairs channel is the first international English-language news channel to broadcast across the globe from the Middle East.  
  
 Al Jazeera's global footprint continues to grow and now broadcasts to more than 220 million households on six continents in more than 100 countries.  
  
 Our channel is broadcast from four strategic broadcast centres: Doha, Kuala Lumpur, London, and Washington DC. Unlike other international channels, we broadcast from our different centres, as the world turns, providing the most comprehensive and contextual news coverage.  
  
 Our mission is to provide independent, impartial news for an international audience and to offer a voice to a diversity of perspectives from under-reported regions.  
  
 In addition, the channel aims to balance the information flow between the South and the North.  
  
 The channel of reference for the Middle East and Africa, Al Jazeera has unique access to some of the world’s most troubled and controversial locations. Our determination and ability to accurately reflect the truth on the ground in regions torn by conflict and poverty has set our content apart."  
  
 Source: Al Jazeera

# SSL certificates - Official Kodi Wiki

SSL certificates
================

From Official Kodi Wiki

[Jump to navigation](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#mw-head)
 [Jump to search](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#searchInput)

Starting with v18 [Leia](https://kodi.wiki/view/Leia "Leia")
, Kodi verifies the certificates of peers in SSL-secured connections. This is very important for security, but might lead to some troubles connecting to [HTTPS](https://kodi.wiki/view/HTTPS "HTTPS")
 and [FTPS](https://kodi.wiki/view/FTP "FTP")
 servers depending on your setup.

For connections to publicly available third-party servers, no problems should be experienced because they use certificates issued by trusted certificate authorities (CAs) and are set up in a correct way (otherwise web browsers would not be able to access them). However, you have to be careful with servers that you manage yourself; see below for the details on how Kodi checks certificates and what steps you might have to take.

Contents
--------

*   [1 Scope](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Scope)
    
*   [2 Checks performed](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Checks_performed)
    *   [2.1 Trust](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Trust)
        
    *   [2.2 Server identity](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Server_identity)
        
*   [3 Trusting your servers](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Trusting_your_servers)
    *   [3.1 Servers accessible via the internet](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Servers_accessible_via_the_internet)
        
    *   [3.2 Servers NOT accessible via the internet](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Servers_NOT_accessible_via_the_internet)
        *   [3.2.1 Adding certificates to the trust store](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Adding_certificates_to_the_trust_store)
            *   [3.2.1.1 Linux](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Linux)
                
            *   [3.2.1.2 All other platforms](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#All_other_platforms)
                
        *   [3.2.2 Disabling the check](https://kodi.wiki/view/SSL_certificates#Disabling_the_check)
            

Scope
-----

Certificate checking (in the context of this wiki page) affects all outgoing SSL-secured connections made by Kodi (both core Kodi and Python add-ons) via the [curl library](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CURL "w:CURL")
. In practice, this means all HTTPS and FTPS protocol requests. The check is performed by curl when initially connecting to a server. If the check fails, the connection will be terminated and the resource in question cannot be used.

Checks performed
----------------

Kodi will check that the certificate of the server

1.  is trusted, and
2.  that it was explicitly issued (by domain name or IP address) for the server you wanted to connect to.

### Trust

SSL trust is conferred by only allowing certificates issued by Certificate Authorities known to thoroughly check the claimed ownership of servers prior to issuance. Lists of such trusted authorities are usually distributed with operating systems and browsers. If this check fails, you will get errors similar to `ERROR: CCurlFile::FillBuffer - Failed: Peer certificate cannot be authenticated with given CA certificates(60)` in your log and connections will fail. There are multiple ways to deal with this when the need arises that are detailed below. For technical details on the check, see [CURLOPT\_SSL\_VERIFYPEER](https://curl.haxx.se/libcurl/c/CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER.html)
.

### Server identity

Verifying the server name in the certificate against the host being connected to is always enabled and cannot be disabled. You have to be careful to ensure that the hostname you enter in Kodi (e.g. as part of an URL or in file source settings) matches the name on the certificate. Otherwise you will get errors similar to `SSL: certificate subject name 'xy' does not match target host name 'real.host.name'` in your log, and connections will fail.

Trusting your servers
---------------------

### Servers accessible via the internet

If your server is accessible via the internet, you can get a certificate from a trusted authority. [Let's Encrypt](https://letsencrypt.org/)
 is one example of such a certificate authority, notable for the fact that it issues such certificates for free (the trade-off being that they must be renewed every 89 days, compared to most other CAs which issue certificates that are valid for at least a year), but any major CA will work.

### Servers NOT accessible via the internet

If your server is not accessible via the internet, you cannot get a certificate from a trusted authority, so you have to create a certificate yourself (known as a _self-signed certificate_). For instructions on how to do this, please refer to the manual of your server software. After that, you have to convince Kodi to trust that certificate.

#### Adding certificates to the trust store

How Kodi determines what certificate authorities to trust depends on your platform.

##### Linux

The certificate store of the operating system (as compiled into the curl library used on the system) is used. The process of adding new certificates to that store depends on your distribution, so please refer to its documentation. For Ubuntu and similar, it is sufficient to copy your certificate (in [DER format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X.690 "w:X.690")
) to `/usr/local/share/ca-certificates/` and then run

sudo update-ca-certificates

.

##### All other platforms

Kodi includes its own bundle of default trusted certificate authorities in the file `system/certs/cacert.pem` of the Kodi installation.

1.  Copy the file to a new location
2.  Add your certificate (in [PEM format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Privacy-Enhanced_Mail "w:Privacy-Enhanced Mail")
    ) to the end of the new file
3.  Set the environment variable `SSL_CERT_FILE` to the location of that new file

This method is also usable on Linux if you do not want to change your system trust store.

#### Disabling the check

If for whatever reason you cannot get a self-signed certificate trusted, there is the _**explicitly discouraged**_ option to disable the check altogether for network file sources. This way, you will lose most of the benefits of using SSL, since man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks are trivially possible. **You have been warned.** To disable the check, add `|verifypeer=false` to the end of the URL or remote path of your source.

Retrieved from "[https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=SSL\_certificates&oldid=241739](https://kodi.wiki/index.php?title=SSL_certificates&oldid=241739)
"

# FireTV Maintenance and Kodi Performance - Official Kodi Wiki

FireTV Maintenance and Kodi Performance
=======================================

From Official Kodi Wiki

[Jump to navigation](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#mw-head)
 [Jump to search](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#searchInput)

Contents
--------

*   [1 An Important Note](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#An_Important_Note)
    
*   [2 What About Issues in Kodi Itself?](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#What_About_Issues_in_Kodi_Itself?)
    *   [2.1 Settings in Kodi](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Settings_in_Kodi)
        
*   [3 FireTV Hardware Issues](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#FireTV_Hardware_Issues)
    *   [3.1 The TV is Interfering with the Fire TV Connection](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#The_TV_is_Interfering_with_the_Fire_TV_Connection)
        
    *   [3.2 Your Unit Is Overheating](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Your_Unit_Is_Overheating)
        
    *   [3.3 Your Network](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Your_Network)
        
    *   [3.4 Your Power Supply](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Your_Power_Supply)
        
    *   [3.5 Your Next Steps](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Your_Next_Steps)
        
*   [4 A General List of FireTV Issues](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#A_General_List_of_FireTV_Issues)
    
*   [5 FireTV Maintenance](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#FireTV_Maintenance)
    *   [5.1 How do I Delete an Application From My FireTV / Stick?](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#How_do_I_Delete_an_Application_From_My_FireTV_/_Stick?)
        
    *   [5.2 Where Can I Clear My Cache in the Kodi App on Fire TV?](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Where_Can_I_Clear_My_Cache_in_the_Kodi_App_on_Fire_TV?)
        
    *   [5.3 Should I Clean Out the APKs After An Installation?](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Should_I_Clean_Out_the_APKs_After_An_Installation?)
        
    *   [5.4 Adjust Your Video Resolution](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Adjust_Your_Video_Resolution)
        
    *   [5.5 Are There Tools To Make This Process Easier?](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Are_There_Tools_To_Make_This_Process_Easier?)
        
*   [6 Related Links](https://kodi.wiki/view/FireTV_Maintenance_and_Kodi_Performance#Related_Links)
    

Many people think that the Fire TV and stick require little or no maintenance, until they try to install and use Kodi (which will tax the processor and available memory, regardless of which version they are using, particularly when streaming movies and videos). They then wonder why Kodi doesn't perform very well, gets memory issues or even crashes. Sometimes this can be alleviated by performing maintenance, which should be done at regular intervals.

  

An Important Note
-----------------

Buffering and stuttering are both part of the video and IPTV world on the net, and sometimes the causes don't lie with your hardware or software. Using links with poor quality videos can cause issues. In addition, servers might be running into bandwidth limits (this is very true of the free video services). Some ISPs are known to throttle the speed of your connection back during certain times.

  

What About Issues in Kodi Itself?
---------------------------------

It seems that no matter which answer you discover on the Net for storage messages, 3 areas in Kodi are mentioned time and again that need to be cleaned regularly. These are

*   Caches
*   Thumbnails
*   Packages

  

### Settings in Kodi

*   To conserve on disk space (especially with the sticks) you can turn off generating thumbnails. Go to Settings -> Video -> File and deselect **Generate Thumbnails**.

*   Hardware acceleration of videos can be problematic, so it's best to disable it. Go to Settings -> Player -> Videos and turn off both Hardware Acceleration options (both surface and the one with no listing).

  

FireTV Hardware Issues
----------------------

### The TV is Interfering with the Fire TV Connection

If you are using the stick, try using the little extension cable first. Putting more distance between the box or stick and the TV is possible with a high quality HDMI cable.

  

### Your Unit Is Overheating

Many sticks have failed due to overheating. If the unit gets too hot, it can, and sometimes does, cause streaming to become erratic or even fail completely. The fix here is easy; make sure there's lots of free space between the Fire TV unit and the TV. Many have added a small office fan to circulate air around the unit.

  

### Your Network

It goes without saying that the faster the data stream, the better your quality of streaming.

You can start by running a speed test. While speedtest.net is one popular choice, many ISPs have their own testing tool . Most websites recommend a minimum of 5 Mbps (megabit per second) speed, but practically any Hi Definition streaming will require at least twice to three times that, depending on the quality of your signal.

Many websites recommend installing an Android wifi analyzer, but this is not really necessary. As of version 5 of the FireTV OS, there is a hidden tool called System X Ray that can help with some diagnostics. See the [Little Known Fire TV Options and Links](https://kodi.wiki/view/Little_Known_Fire_TV_Options_and_Links "Little Known Fire TV Options and Links")
 article for the link that describes it and how to get it, along with a link to a free FireTV app that can provide additional information.

  

### Your Power Supply

This is particularly important with the Sticks. If you are using a second hand supply (not the original OEM) that doesn't supply sufficient voltage and current, you are bound to run into trouble. Amazon has a page of these devices [here](http://tinyurl.com/yc5s7x29)
.

  

### Your Next Steps

If you've done all of this, and still have issues, it's time to dive into doing some maintenance on the FireTV device itself.

  

A General List of FireTV Issues
-------------------------------

*   You've got lots of applications that you no longer use. These eat up memory space and should be deleted. They can be reloaded if you find you need them later.
*   When you exit an application, it's actually not shut down; instead it's kept in a queued state, maintained in a cache, so that it launches faster the next time you use it. The problem is that if you have a lot of applications, after a while, you will seriously degrade the amount of free memory.
*   Another issue lies in something we've likely all done; you didn't like an application, so you uninstalled it. The problem is that this can leave junk files behind; and that eats at your available free space. Even downloads and installs using a sideload can leave junk behind.

  

FireTV Maintenance
------------------

### How do I Delete an Application From My FireTV / Stick?

Go to **Settings**, then **Applications** then **Manage Installed Applications**. Then select the application you want to remove. First use **Force Stop**, then **Clear Data** (which removes user data and any settings), then **Uninstall**. After you completed removing your apps, you will want to use [Clean Master](http://tinyurl.com/yd4c4xak)
 to wipe junk files and reclaim the space you just cleared.

  

### Where Can I Clear My Cache in the Kodi App on Fire TV?

Go to **Settings**, then **Applications** then **Manage Installed Applications**. Go down to Kodi on this panel and use **Force Stop** and **Clear Cache**. In fact you should perform these steps on any software that you have installed or use often. **Never** use the **Clear Data** option unless you wish to delete all of your settings and data from that application. If you do this in Kodi, it's similar to doing a fresh install.

  

### Should I Clean Out the APKs After An Installation?

Yes; this is particularly true if you are using a Stick. Sometimes the application will offer to delete it after the installation is complete; if not, you can use an utility like Kodi's **[file manager](https://kodi.wiki/view/File_manager "File manager")
** to drop the apk. They are usually found in the Downloads folder.

  

### Adjust Your Video Resolution

*   If you have the latest 5.2.4.1 firmware, you will find that playing a 1080p video at 24Hz resolution doesn't work well. There is a bug in the update, and it's discussed [here](http://www.aftvnews.com/fire-tv-update-5-2-4-1-causing-poor-24p-video-playback-in-mrmc-kodi-and-spmc/)
    
*   Sometimes buffering and stuttering can be caused by a mismatch between the resolution the server sends the video (say at 1080p), while your FireTV is set at something lower. Normally the FireTV will adjust to this, but if you find it isn't working well, there's a little known trick for setting it manually [here](http://www.aftvnews.com/how-to-access-hidden-resolution-options-on-the-fire-tv/)
    
*   You should also check your user's manual to see whether the resolution and refresh rate you want to use are supported on your TV or monitor. It's usually very easy to reset it if you need to change it.

  

### Are There Tools To Make This Process Easier?

There is a great deal of information available that shows you how to optimize your FireTV / Stick. Most involve going into the **Manage Installed Applications** (as described above) and turning various settings off, such as the Whispersync (assuming you aren't using it), and collecting data. Things like this add additional load to the CPU that, particularly in the case of the Sticks, really can't handle the load without bogging down.

  

Related Links
-------------

*   [Android/ATV2 Maintenance Tool](https://forum.kodi.tv/showthread.php?tid=228075)
     from Kodi TV Forum
*   [Caches explained](https://kodi.wiki/view/Caches_explained "Caches explained")
    
*   [Fire Stick Extremely Slow](https://www.amazon.com/forum/fire?_encoding=UTF8&cdForum=Fx2L8EBNTOXFSA7&cdThread=Tx999T9F3P9P9O)
    
*   You will find many websites mention modifying the advancedsettings.xml file as a buffering solution. This [page](https://kodi.wiki/view/Advancedsettings.xml "Advancedsettings.xml")
     describes this file in detail

Alternative keymaps for Fire TV remote

From Official Kodi Wiki

| [![](https://kodi.wiki/images/a/aa/Home_icon_grey.png)](https://kodi.wiki/view/Main_Page "Main Page") |     |     | ![▶](https://kodi.wiki/images/5/5f/TriangleArrow-Right.png) [Amazon Fire TV](https://kodi.wiki/view/Amazon_Fire_TV "Amazon Fire TV") | ![▶](https://kodi.wiki/images/5/5f/TriangleArrow-Right.png) **Alternative keymaps for Fire TV remote** |

Alternative [keymaps](https://kodi.wiki/view/Keymaps "Keymaps")
 for the [Amazon Fire TV](https://kodi.wiki/view/Amazon_Fire_TV "Amazon Fire TV")
 remote, as suggested by the community.

--------

*   [1 Installing keymaps](https://kodi.wiki/view/Alternative_keymaps_for_Fire_TV_remote#Installing_keymaps)

*   [2 Keymap 1](https://kodi.wiki/view/Alternative_keymaps_for_Fire_TV_remote#Keymap_1)
